subject: Renewal: Hybrid EU residency + APAC staging — amendment and runbook
messages:
From: Simon Leung <simon.leung@medispanhealth.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medispanhealth.com
Date: Mon, 1 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal: Hybrid EU residency + APAC staging — initial ask

Hi Irene / Lauren,

We’re starting the renewal conversation for our Redwood contract (renewal window opens Jan 15). Usage is trending up — we expect approx +30% token volume next 12 months, with heavier EU traffic due to a new pilot in Germany. Key asks from our side: 

- Confirm an amendment to make EU the primary residency for our tenant (data-at-rest + processing in EU nodes).
- Add APAC warm-standby (staged burst) to support regional failover and a phased rollout in Q2.
- Updated pricing for the hybrid setup and any SLA changes for regional failover.
- A short runbook outlining failover test cadence and data residency verification steps required for our audits.

Can you share a draft amendment and an ops runbook? Procurement copied on this thread — they’ll need pricing and a DocuSign-ready amendment. I’ve attached our internal forecast (Medispan_2026_usage.csv) — high-level numbers at the bottom.

Proposed times for a 30–45m call this week: Tue 11–1 PT or Wed 9–11 PT.

Thanks,
Simon
Simon Leung
Head of Platform Engineering, Medispan Health
[samples of attachments: Medispan_2026_usage.csv (csv)]

From: irene.choi@redwood.com
To: Simon Leung <simon.leung@medispanhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@medispanhealth.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Dec 2025 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: Hybrid EU residency + APAC staging — initial ask

Hi Simon — thanks for the clear summary and the forecast. Happy to run point on this. High level next steps we propose: 

1) Draft an amendment that:
   - Makes EU nodes the primary residency (data processing & storage in EU only for labeled traffic).
   - Adds an APAC warm-standby pool that can be burstable for traffic spikes and failover.
   - Defines a failover SLA (activation time / RTO) and a verification cadence for residency audits.

2) Ops runbook: Mina (cc’d) will author runbook items (failover test plan, KV cache handling, audit log samples, KMS key routing).

3) Commercials: I’ll have Ben share the pricing delta and suggested term change (12-month renewal with optional top-up).

I’ve attached two initial artifacts: redwood-amendment-v1.docx (draft language) and redwood-capacity-plan-120k-tokens.xlsx (proposed reserved capacity). Please review and let us know which call window works.

Proposed call: Tue 12/2 at 11:00 PT (30m). If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[samples of attachments: redwood-amendment-v1.docx (docx), redwood-capacity-plan-120k-tokens.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: Simon Leung <simon.leung@medispanhealth.com>, irene.choi@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Dec 2025 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: Hybrid EU residency + APAC staging — ops runbook items

Simon — nice to meet you over email. I’m Mina on the Redwood Ops/Onboarding team. I took a pass at the runbook tasks; below are the items I’ll include and the details we’ll need from your side: 

- Verification & audit steps (what we’ll produce):
  * Sample audit logs showing EU processing (retention: 13 months by default; can adjust by PO).
  * KV cache migration plan for a controlled cutover (timeline and expected cold-cache penalty).

- Failover test cadence:
  * Staging test: monthly simulated failover (APAC warm-standby receives mirrored traffic for 30m).
  * Full failover drill: quarterly, formal runbook activation, rollback plan.

- Networking / KMS questions (items for Medispan):
  * Do you require customer-managed KMS keys for EU nodes (Y/N)?
  * Any IP allowlist restrictions for APAC bursts we should pre-authorize?

I’m attaching a short SLA exception request template that we’ll use if you need faster RTOs during failover (SLA-exception-request.pdf). If you can confirm the KMS preference and an IP block, I’ll lock down the runbook and include examples for your auditors.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Onboarding & Reliability, Redwood Inference
[attachment stub: SLA-exception-request.pdf (pdf)]

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: Simon Leung <simon.leung@medispanhealth.com>, procurement@medispanhealth.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Dec 2025 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: Hybrid EU residency + APAC staging — commercial summary

Simon / Procurement — quick commercial summary based on the forecast and proposed architecture: 

- Term: 12 months (renewal effective Jan 15, 2026)
- EU reserved capacity: 4 x V100-equivalent GPUs (baseline) — covers primary processing for EU-labeled traffic
- APAC warm-standby: cold reserve with burst to 2 x GPUs for emergency / pilot support

Pricing delta (per month, net of existing credits):
- EU reserved pool: $28,000
- APAC warm-standby (on-demand reserve fee): $6,500
- One-time amendment & onboarding fee: $12,000

Total monthly delta: $34,500 (first month includes onboarding fee). We can structure as a committed UCapacity add-on or as a fixed monthly surcharge — open to procurement preference.

Next steps:
1) If the above looks OK, countersign the attached amendment (redwood-amendment-v1.docx) via DocuSign here: https://www.docusign.com/en/transaction/abc123
2) Procurement to confirm PO path & KMS preference so Ops can finalize the runbook.

Simon — happy to jump on a short call to walk procurement through the DocuSign and payment options.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
[sample attachment: redwood-amendment-v1.docx]

From: procurement@medispanhealth.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2025 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: Hybrid EU residency + APAC staging — procurement review

Thanks Ben / Irene — procurement here. We reviewed the amendment and the economics. We are generally aligned but have one minor redline request: change the failover SLA activation window from 5m to 15m in section 4.2 (we need a slightly longer window to validate traffic routing on our side).

We will:
- Return a redlined amendment by EOD tomorrow if the 15m SLA window is acceptable.
- Route the PO once DocuSign is complete (we prefer a single PO referencing DEAL-8342-MSH).

Forwarded for visibility: please confirm if Redwood accepts the 15m activation window or if that requires an SLA-exception (and if so, the associated fee).
